title: The Way Ahead For US Hyperscalers
gist: Gavekal frames Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet's rebranding from 'Magnificent Seven' to 'hyperscalers' as evidence of a fundamental business-model shift: breakneck AI capex is now eroding the free cash flow that once let their shares outperform regardless of the investment climate, with four unnamed scenarios set to determine future share-price direction.

insights.claim: Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet have cycled through a succession of investment-theme labels over the years -- platform companies, then FAANGs, then the Magnificent Seven -- and are now being recast as 'hyperscalers', signaling a real shift in business model rather than just rebranding.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors tracking these names by their old 'Mag-7' investment thesis (low capex, high FCF, climate-agnostic outperformance) are working from an outdated framework that no longer describes the businesses.
insights.quote: generating a succession of catchy investment themes, first as platform companies, next as FAANGs, then as the Magnificent Seven

insights.claim: For years, the low-capital-expenditure, high-cash-flow business model of these big tech companies let their share prices perform well almost regardless of the broader investment climate; Gavekal states that this business model and its associated investment narrative have now changed.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A structural break from a decade-long pattern of climate-agnostic outperformance implies these stocks may become more macro- and capex-sensitive going forward, a material shift for portfolio positioning.
insights.quote: their business model of rapid innovation, low capital expenditure and strong cash flows allowed their share prices to perform well almost regardless of the investment climate

themes.theme: AI Capex Race and Shrinking Free Cash Flow

insights.claim: Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet are investing capital at breakneck pace in AI chips, data centers, and supporting infrastructure as part of a race to secure AI dominance.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Confirms the AI infrastructure buildout among the largest hyperscalers is accelerating rather than plateauing, with direct implications for chip and data-center supply chains.
insights.quote: in the race to secure AI dominance they are investing capital at breakneck pace in the necessary AI chips, data centers and supporting infrastructure

insights.claim: As a direct result of the breakneck AI infrastructure spending, hyperscalers' free cash flows are dwindling -- reversing the strong-cash-generation dynamic that previously supported their valuations.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Falling free cash flow at companies once prized for cash generation warrants close monitoring of capex-to-FCF ratios as a leading indicator of stress in hyperscaler valuations.
insights.quote: their free cash flows are dwindling

insights.claim: Gavekal argues that from this point forward, the relative trajectories of capex and free cash flow -- not the old low-capex/high-FCF model -- will shape hyperscalers' businesses and determine their share-price performance, and lays out four main scenarios for how this could unfold.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should watch the capex-versus-FCF trend as the primary variable for hyperscaler share prices going forward; the specific four scenarios are gated behind Gavekal's paywall and were not disclosed in this teaser.
insights.quote: the relative trajectories of their capex and free cash flow will shape their businesses and determine the performance of their share prices
